Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros  i'm samira, i'm leading the AE motion here at Redwood. we have ethan from our se team. how's your side?
[00:12] Maya (Helion): hi hi, maya here, head of ml at helion. liam is our cto and priya is on infra. thanks for taking the time.
[00:18] Liam (Helion): yeah thanks, short intro from me. excited to dig in  we've got a couple of use cases.
[00:25] Ethan (Redwood SE): great, thanks. goal for the call is to scope the poc: success criteria, workload sizing, what benchmarks we run and timeline. we'll try to capture QPS, concurrency, and token distributions so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated and a benchmark plan.
[00:38] Maya: sounds good. to summarize our use case quick  core app is a conversational finance assistant for merchants and internal ops, and a second feature is transaction enrichment (categorization + anomaly flags). the conversational queries are usually short but sometimes include long receipts pasted in.
[00:53] [00:50] Maya: for numbers, our poisson-ish traffic spike pattern is about 3 qps average across US region, with peak bursts to ~45 qps during batch syncs and peak checkout flows. baseline concurrency for webchat is about 30 concurrent sessions, peaks hitting 200 for a few minutes during promotions.
[01:09] Samira: ok that's helpful  can you clarify tokens per request on those two flows?
[01:15] Maya: sure. for chat normal: input tokens avg 30-60, output tokens 40-80. for receipt ingestion the input can be 800-2,400 tokens (users paste full receipt), output summary typically 80-200 tokens. transaction enrichment payloads are small: input ~120 tokens, output ~30 tokens.
[01:32] Priya (Helion): i should add latency requirement  for chat we're targeting 200-400ms p50, p95 under 1.2s is acceptable. receipts can be async  5-10s ok but prefer quicker. enrichment is p50 <200ms.
[01:45] Ethan: ok good constraints. that gives us the distributions we need. quick note  transcription here may screw up numbers but we'll follow-up with a spreadsheet.
[01:54] [02:00] Liam: curious on recommendation: hosted api vs dedicated. we care about cost but also data isolation; for PCI scope we prefer not to send receipts to a multi-tenant hosted model, unclear on that.
[02:12] Samira: totally, and able to support both. typically we recommend: start with hosted for fast time-to-value for chat and enrichment, and use a dedicated pool for receipts or anything that must be in a private tenancy. if you have strict PCI needs you may prefer private deployment or Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering.
[02:29] Maya: ok that fits what we were thinking. for the poc we'd like to validate: 1) that latency SLOs hold under peaks, 2) that model quality meets our prompts (we'll share eval set), and 3) that economics are reasonable  tokens per request cost extrapolated to monthly.
[02:44] Ethan: perfect, that's a sane set. for benchmarks we propose: synthetic replay of 2 weeks of traffic (anonymized), cut into a 1-hour stress window to hit peak qps, plus steady-state 24-hour run to measure cost and p95 tail. we'll also run controlled token-distribution tests: short chats, receipts batch, enrichment microbenchmarks.
[03:04] Maya: that sounds right. what about model selection? we want an open model with quantization to save cost but not lose quality on NER/categorization.
[03:12] Ethan: we can recommend a few model families  we'll surface Redwood-verified profiles: a smaller quantized 7B-ish for enrichment (fast, cheap), a mid-size 33B quantized for chat, and maybe a non-quantized 70B variant for receipts if you need best accuracy. we'll include model latency and per-token cost estimates in the bench plan.
[03:29] [03:30] Priya: network  if we do Dedicated with VPC peering, what are the egress patterns? do you host in our VPC or you route across a private link?
[03:38] Ethan: for Redwood Dedicated we provision reserved GPU pools in a customer-isolated tenancy with VPC peering or private link options. traffic stays within the peered network and audit logs are exported to your SIEM. we'll attach our network runbook.
[03:48] Liam: ok good. compliance  we need SOC2 docs + encryption at rest keys.
[03:52] Samira: yes we'll share SOC2 report and KMS/HSM integration notes. for Private deployments we can support customer-managed KMS.
[04:00] Maya: timeline  ideally a 4-week poc: week 0 onboarding and traffic handoff, week 1 baseline benchmarks, week 2 scale/stress, week 3 quality/regression evaluation + economics. is that realistic?
[04:12] Ethan: yep that's realistic given we have traffic in 48 hours. if you can provide 2 weeks of sample logs (anonymized) and the eval prompts, we can prep the benchmark harness and spin up a dedicated pool in the poc timeframe.
[04:24] Samira: we'll prepare pricing scenarios: hosted usage, 3-month reserved dedicated commit, and a private deployment estimate. also include potential burst credits.
[04:33] [04:30] Maya: can you outline success criteria in one line? we'll want to present to execs.
[04:38] Samira: sure  success = (1) p95 latency within your SLOs across the three workloads during peak replay, (2) model accuracy on your evaluation prompts meeting the threshold you set, and (3) projected monthly unit cost within the budget range you'll give us. we'll put exact numbers in the SOW.
[04:53] Liam: about the accuracy threshold  we'll define pass/fail. for enrichment we need 95% precision on category labels, for receipts summary we'll do a human eval threshold and for chat we'll track top-level NPS from internal testers.
[05:07] Ethan: noted  we'll include those metrics in the benchmark plan and the eval harness. small note: during stress runs caching and prefix cache behavior matter a lot for economics; can you share your prompt templating patterns?
[05:19] Maya: yes we use a fixed prefix system for contextual info (merchant id, last 10 transactions) and then append user prompt. about 40% of chat requests hit repeat prefixes, so caching should help.
[05:31] Samira: great  caching and batching profiles will be part of the cost extrapolation. we'll run experiments with and without KV/prefix caching to show delta.
[05:41] Priya: we also need to validate concurrency ceilings per GPU; our SRE wants to know concurrency per model instance and how the autoscaler behaves at burst.
[05:50] Ethan: we'll measure max in-flight tokens per GPU, effective QPS at various concurrency levels, and show autoscaler metrics under your burst profile. we'll also capture tail latency and queuing behaviour.
[06:02] [06:00] Maya: ok what about data retention/logging? we need logs for debugging but only for 14 days, then purge.
[06:09] Samira: we can configure log retention and provide a flow for log export to your account; retention settings and deletion policies will be part of the poc config.
[06:18] Liam: is there any limit on prompt size for streaming responses? sometimes receipts are huge.
[06:22] Ethan: model limits apply, but we support chunking and streaming; for very large receipts we recommend chunk+summarize pipeline or using the dedicated large-context model variant. we'll include architecture patterns in the doc.
[06:34] Maya: example numbers i'd like to include in the bench plan: steady qps 3, 95th burst 45 qps, concurrency baseline 30, peak concurrency 200, average token distribution per workload (chat 30/60, enrichment 120/30, receipt 1000/120).
[06:51] Samira: we'll use those as our initial inputs. can you share a CSV with per-request tokens and timestamps?
[06:56] Maya: yes we'll export anonymized records. note that some records have internal party names  we'll scrub PII.
[07:03] Ethan: perfect. for benchmarks we'll run: short chat microbench (100k requests over 1 hour), receipt batch stress (simulate 200 concurrent within a 10-minute storm), and continuous 24-hour replay at average qps for cost extrapolation. we'll also provide a reproducible bench harness and results dashboard.
[07:22] [07:30] Priya: network checklist from our side: open ports for private link, TLS cert exchange, and STS for service accounts. we'll confirm specifics after we see the runbook.
[07:39] Samira: we'll send the runbook and a short checklist for your infra team.
[07:44] Maya: ok what's the expected cost delta between quantized and non-quantized? ballpark numbers are fine.
[07:51] Ethan: ballpark: quantized 7B can be 4-6x cheaper per token compared to non-quantized 70B, with throughput gains. mid-size quantized models (30-40B) often hit a good quality/cost sweet spot  roughly 2x cheaper than full 70B, numbers depend on batching and cache rates. we'll run both in bench.
[08:10] Samira: anything else from your side?
[08:12] Liam: just to confirm timeline  if we hand off logs by monday (2027-01-25), kickoff 2027-01-27, can we have preliminary results by week 2?
[08:22] Ethan: yes we can deliver baseline bench results within 5 business days of kickoff, scale/stress measurements by day 10, and final evaluation + cost extrap by day 20.

[08:37] Samira: we'll include that.
